classification.difficultyReason: Measure each diameter, halve it and substitute into the circumference formula.

content.prompt: Use your ruler to measure (approximately) the diameter of a 20c coin in millimetres. Write down the radius and find the circumference of the coin, rounding the circumference to one decimal place. Repeat the exercise with a 10c coin and a 5c coin.

answer.short: Measurements vary. Sample answers: 20c: $d\approx28$ mm, $r\approx14$ mm, $C\approx88.0$ mm; 10c: $d\approx23.6$ mm, $r\approx11.8$ mm, $C\approx74.1$ mm; 5c: $d\approx19$ mm, $r\approx9.5$ mm, $C\approx59.7$ mm.
answer.worked:
Use each measured diameter in $r=\frac{d}{2}$ and $C=\pi d$. Using $\pi\approx3.14$, sample calculations are:

20c:
$$\begin{align*}r&=28\div2=14\text{ mm}\\C&\approx3.14\times28\\C&\approx88.0\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$
10c:
$$\begin{align*}r&=23.6\div2=11.8\text{ mm}\\C&\approx3.14\times23.6\\C&\approx74.1\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$
5c:
$$\begin{align*}r&=19\div2=9.5\text{ mm}\\C&\approx3.14\times19\\C&\approx59.7\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$
Circumferences are rounded to one decimal place. Results depend on the measurements.
